title: SMILE PRO: The New Paradigm in Corneal Refractive Surgery
summary: SMILE Pro (Small Incision Lenticule Extraction) represents the evolution of refractive surgery using femtosecond laser technology. It offers a flapless, minimally invasive procedure for the correction of myopia and myopic astigmatism with faster laser treatment times and advanced centration guidance.

sections.title: Definition & Core Technology
sections.content: SMILE Pro is an advanced refractive procedure using the VisuMax 800 femtosecond laser (Carl Zeiss Meditec). Unlike traditional LASIK, which requires a 20mm circumference flap, SMILE Pro creates a refractive lenticule within the corneal stroma through a small incision (< 2mm). The 'Pro' iteration features a faster 2kHz laser repetition rate, enabling treatment times < 10 seconds, and utilizes OcuLign/CentraLign technology for cyclotorsion compensation.

sections.title: Clinical Advantages Over Femto-LASIK
content: Biomechanical stability: Preserves anterior stroma integrity
Dry eye: Lower incidence of post-op dry eye due to sub-basal nerve plexus sparing
Flapless: No risk of flap displacement or interface epithelial ingrowth
Precision: Superior centration via automated cyclotorsion compensation

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Process Flow
content: 1. Docking: Contact lens interface alignment with active cyclotorsion control.
2. Lenticule Creation: Femtosecond laser pulses create the posterior then anterior surfaces of the refractive lenticule.
3. Incision: A small 2mm side-cut incision is created.
4. Dissection: Surgeon separates the anterior and posterior planes using a spatula.
5. Extraction: The lenticule is removed manually through the incision.

sections.title: Red Flags: Contraindications
content: Forme fruste keratoconus or ectatic disease

sections.title: Recent Landmark Evidence
content: The SILK (Small Incision Lenticule Keratomileusis) studies demonstrate non-inferiority of SMILE vs. FS-LASIK in visual acuity outcomes.
Meta-analyses highlight significant improvements in corneal sub-basal nerve fiber density at 6 months compared to LASIK cohorts.
Recent focus is shifting toward 'hyperopic SMILE' using custom lenticule profiles currently in clinical trials.
